# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Emerson Brooks**
[Street address]
[City], Iowa [ZIP]
[Phone] · [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** UnitedHealthcare — Appeals
Submitted through my member account at member.uhc.com, or to the appeal address printed on my denial notice
(Member Services: the number on my ID card)

**RE: Appeal of denial dated August 4, 2026**
- **Member:** Emerson Brooks
- **Member ID:** W628799962
- **Reference number:** POC-9AB63CFCDF-18778
- **Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
- **Plan:** UnitedHealthcare (Commercial/ACA), state of Iowa
- **Governing policy:** *Surgery of the Shoulder (2026T0556FF)*, effective January 1, 2026 — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-shoulder.pdf
- **This appeal is timely:** the notice states my appeal must be received by January 31, 2027.

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti of orthopedic surgery, requested for me. The denial notice dated August 4, 2026 says the request was denied because the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking UnitedHealthcare to reconsider that decision, to review the clinical record described below, and — if anything is still considered missing — to tell me in writing exactly which document or finding is needed so that it can be supplied.

My surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed. The records in the prior authorization packet set out the diagnosis, the treatments I have already tried, and how limited my shoulder has become.

## The plan's own policy, and how my records line up with it

The policy that governs this request, *Surgery of the Shoulder (2026T0556FF)*, states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the shoulder is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

So shoulder surgery is covered under my plan when the clinical circumstances support it. The policy then directs the reader to its medical necessity criteria:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the:"

> "o Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Shoulder o Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Shoulder (Adolescent) o Joint Replacement, Shoulder o Removal and Replacement or Revision, Joint Replacement, Shoulder Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

The policy also confirms that these outside criteria are part of how my plan makes these decisions:

> "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits."

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about the limits of what I have. The excerpt above ends in a colon and points to separate criteria sets — including "Joint Replacement, Shoulder," which is the category my requested surgery falls under. That criteria text is held in InterQual and was not reproduced in the policy pages available to me. **I therefore cannot quote the specific clinical rule that was applied to my case, and I am not attempting to. I am asking the plan to provide it** (see the request below). Beyond the sentences quoted above, I am not characterizing what the policy requires, because I have not been shown it.

One criteria set in the policy that I can quote reads:

> "≥ age 40, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) imaging showing a full-thickness massive rotator cuff tear measuring ≥ 5cm and involving ≥ 2 tendons within nine months of study enrollment, functional deltoid muscle and preserved passive ROM on physical examination, VAS score greater than 30mm and who underwent failed conservative therapy for at least four months."

I am pointing this out because my records do not describe a rotator cuff tear at all — my CT confirms an **intact rotator cuff**. My shoulder problem is joint destruction, not a cuff tear, so this particular pathway does not appear to describe my situation, and I would ask that my request not be measured against it.

The policy also states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand that submitting records does not by itself guarantee coverage. But the denial rests entirely on documentation being incomplete, and the following was documented in the prior authorization packet:

| What the record shows | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Nine months of progressive shoulder pain, not relieved by rest | Clinical summary in the prior authorization packet |
| Supervised physical therapy for range of motion and periscapular strengthening — 10 weeks, March 30, 2026 to June 8, 2026, 18 visits completed | Physical therapy discharge note |
| NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief | Clinical summary |
| Corticosteroid injection on March 30, 2026, giving 3 weeks of partial relief | Clinical summary |
| Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) on May 23, 2026: complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid | Imaging report |
| CT confirming an intact rotator cuff | Imaging report |
| Exam: glenohumeral crepitus; active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees; external rotation limited to 10 degrees; cuff strength intact | Physical examination |
| Function: I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side | Clinical summary |
| No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker | Clinical summary |
| Requesting surgeon: Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery | Prior authorization packet |

That is a documented diagnosis on imaging, a documented course of non-surgical treatment with dates and visit counts, documented exam findings, and documented loss of everyday function. If a specific item is still considered missing, I would genuinely like to know what it is, because I am willing to obtain it.

## Request for the criteria that were applied to my case

**I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule or criterion UnitedHealthcare relied on to deny this request — specifically, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination.** The policy routes medical necessity decisions for shoulder joint replacement to InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document, so I have no way to obtain it myself. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide the specific rule or criterion relied upon for an adverse determination at no cost to me. The plan holds that document; I am asking it to send it to me so that I can respond to the actual standard being applied. I am also requesting the clinical reviewer's credentials and the documentation checklist used, if one exists.

I would ask that the appeal timeline account for my receiving that material, so that I have a fair chance to address it.

## Closing

Please reconsider the denial of CPT 23472 and approve the total shoulder replacement my surgeon has documented as necessary. If the decision remains unfavorable, please send me a written explanation that identifies each specific item of documentation found to be missing, along with the criteria text requested above and information about my rights to further review, including external review.

I can be reached at [phone] or [email], and my surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone] if additional records would help. Thank you for taking a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Brooks**
